chunks: Three breaths during drinking is better than one breath.

key_terms.أَفْضَل: Better/more virtuous; comparative form indicating a recommended preference
key_terms.أَنْفَاس: Breaths/sips; the plural of nafas, referring to pauses taken during drinking

ai.seo_question: Is it better to drink water in three breaths or one in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that drinking in three separate breaths is superior to drinking in one continuous breath. This is a recommendation rooted in the adab (etiquette) of eating and drinking in Islamic tradition, where measured, deliberate consumption was considered both healthier and more mindful. The original audience of this jurisprudential guidance — scholars and students of fiqh — would have understood this as a recommended (mustahabb) practice contributing to proper Islamic manners.
